comments.author: @UpnorthHere
comments.text:
This is really sad. There is literally no such thing as a provisional patent. There is a provisional APPLICATION for a patent. It gives you NO ENFORCEABLE RIGHTS. Only after you file a non-provisional application, have it examined and issued as a patent do you get any patent rights. A patent also does NOT "give you right to make what you patented". It only gives you the right to prevent others from making, using, selling or importing your invention, as long as it is issued and enforceable in that country. If your invention also infringes anyone else's patents, you still need licenses from each and every one of those.  
"Making sure nobody else already has a patent" is only the narrowest tip of a gigantic iceberg that can sink your patent. Your invention must be new and non-obvious in light of EVERYTHING ever disclosed in any publication anywhere in the world or used in public  by anyone, whether or not it was ever patented.  
If you mess up your provisional application, you're kidding yourself and your resulting patent (if one is ever issued) will be perhaps LESS VALUABLE than if you had never filed a provisional application.

If you have a valuable invention you owe it to yourself to get actual valuable advice from a professional patent attorney and otherwise not waste your $75 to file garbage.  "Patent pending" is often a stupid reason to file, unless your investors are also stupid and don't know how to read your provisional applications before giving you their money.
